Title: Israel's determination to disarm Hamas is 'absolute': military chief

Summary: 
Israel's military chief, Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir, stated on Wednesday, December 31, 2025, that Israel's determination to disarm Hamas is 'absolute,' calling 2026 a 'decisive year' for Israel's security. Zamir made the remarks during a visit to troops in Gaza, emphasizing that Israel will not allow Hamas to rebuild its military capabilities. This follows a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump, who also stressed that Hamas must disarm quickly, warning, 'If they don't disarm as they agreed to do, then there will be hell to pay for them.' The truce in Gaza, which began on October 10, 2025, has largely halted hostilities, but concerns persist about both sides slow-walking the second stage of the ceasefire. Under this stage, Israel is to gradually withdraw from Gaza, Hamas is to surrender its weapons, an interim authority is to assume governance, and an international stabilisation force (ISF) is to be deployed. Despite the agreement, both sides have accused each other of frequent ceasefire violations.

Regarding the collection of truck taxes on aid and goods entering Gaza, the sources said control over shipments will be transferred to a technocratic committee, preventing Hamas from receiving these funds. Concerning Hamas-affiliated civil employees, the council possesses extensive databases with names and details, and anyone listed will be barred from working in the new civilian police or security forces. The sources also noted that Turkey and Qatar are included in the council due to their significant influence over Hamas, which is essential for pressuring the group to disarm. Title: Israel, U.S. Give Hamas Two-Month Deadline to Disarm or Face Consequences

Summary: 
Israel and the United States have issued a two-month deadline to Hamas to fully disarm, marking a significant escalation in pressure on the group. According to Yisrael Hayom, the agreement was reached during an overnight meeting at Mar-a-Lago between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump. Under the terms, Hamas must dismantle its military capabilities, including its weapons stockpiles, command structure, and the extensive underground tunnel network in Gaza, within approximately 60 days. Israeli and American teams are developing mutually agreed criteria for 'practical disarmament.' Israeli officials remain skeptical of Hamas’s willingness to comply, citing the group’s public rejection of disarmament and the likelihood of only offering symbolic concessions. Both nations agree that any outcome short of full disarmament is unacceptable. If the deadline is not met, responsibility for next steps will revert to Israel, potentially leading to renewed and intensified military operations in Gaza. The two-month ultimatum represents one of the clearest joint statements yet from Israel and the U.S. regarding Hamas, with diplomatic channels open but patience limited, as the clock is now running.
